name: Un Mes Un Fan Tres 1+1=3 Cava Brut
description: This Non‑Vintage 1+1=3 Cava Brut envelopes the senses with bright orchard fruits and a whisper of minerality, expressing a fresh and lively personality rooted in Penedès tradition. The precise blend of Macabeo with Xarel‑lo and Parellada yields a balanced wine of fine bubble and chalky saline undertones, evoking old‑world elegance with everyday charm.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in tulip‑shaped flutes to highlight its persistent mousse. Superb as an aperitif or alongside simple seafood fare like tapas or paella.
palate: crisp citrus with fine mineral undertow

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Oakville Napa Valley
description: A striking expression of Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon, this 2018 Acclaimed captures ripe dark fruit nuance and oak‑inspired warmth with refined restraint, offering a polished profile that honours its Napa Valley heritage. It displays structural harmony and textural elegance befitting a wine crafted from a celebrated vintage and a first‑rate hillside site.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below ambient to showcase its layered fruit and balanced tannins. Pairs beautifully with rich red meats or aged cheeses.
palate: rich black plum and black cherry core with mocha subtlety
finish: bold, firm texture with lasting oak‑tinged depth

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Acentor Garnacha Do Calatayud
description: This 2021 Acentor Garnacha by Isaac Fernández Selección hails from Calatayud in Aragón, Spain, crafted from century‑old bush vines planted on iron‑rich red clay at high elevation. It offers a layered aromatic tapestry of tar, allspice‑dusted red currants and cran‑pomegranate, unfolding into a dense yet lithe palate of citrus rind, fresh red fruits and saline mineral tension, finishing with depth and salinity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in medium‑bodied red glass to accentuate freshness. It pairs beautifully with roasted lamb, grilled chorizo or tomato‑based stews, inviting both meatiness and spice.
aroma: tar, allspice dusted red currants, cran‑pomegranate
palate: fresh, fat, juicy citrus rind and saline red fruits

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Acentor Rioja
description: An elegant expression from Rioja’s heartland this wine offers a seductive balance of ripe black fruits and subtle tobacco framed by gently integrated oak spices. Its refined structure unfolds with melting tannins and an earthy persistency that lingers graciously.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to reveal its nuanced fruit character; pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops, roasted mushrooms, or aged Manchego.
palate: ripe fruit driven with soft tannic support

name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A wine of elegant gravitas from Napa Valley, the 2018 Acre Cabernet Sauvignon showcases dark plum and cassis aromas layered with leather, earth, and an exotic spice‑box perfume. Its palate unfolds with silky tannins and echoes of black cherry, cedar, black tea, and pencil‑lead, culminating in a supple, refined finish that speaks to its organic origins in Yountville.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in large Bordeaux glasses allow gentle aeration pair with grilled rib‑eye, truffle‑accented mushroom dishes, or aged Manchego.
palate: silky tannins black cherry cedar black tea pencil‑lead

name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A refined expression of Napa Valley cabernet with regal poise that speaks of a storied vineyard heritage. The aromatic tapestry weaves bright black cherry and raspberry threads with sage and cedar nuances falling into a palate shaped by boysenberry, plum, graphite and a whisper of blood orange, all anchored by balanced tannins and vivid acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in a large-bowled glass to allow the raspberry and cedar notes to blossom; pairs exquisitely with rib‑eye steak or aged gouda.
palate: boysenberry and graphite underpinned by lively acidity

name: Adamvs Quintvs Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain
description: A profoundly concentrated mountain Cabernet drawn from the steep, volcanic ash–lined slopes of Howell Mountain this 2018 Quintvs is an aristocratic and powerfully structured wine with a heart of wild cherry and blackberry framed by subtle woodland florals and forest floor nuance. Elegant yet forceful its texture is velvety and mineral‑infused with a vertical drive suggesting both youth and poised maturity.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a firm decant to soften the stately tannins and pair with richly roasted lamb or game dishes; its structure will reward cellaring of ten to fifteen years.
aroma: wild cherry, blackberry, lavender, wild rose, forest floor
palate: ripe fruit, fresh bay, wild sage, mineral‑laced drive

name: Gran Vinum Esencia Divina Albarino Do Rias Baixas
description: A refined Albariño from Rías Baixas that exudes pale straw hues and delicate green reflections, lifted by white blossoms, elderflower and orchard fruits. The palate unfolds with a gentle touch of sweetness and persistent floral echoes, its poised acidity imparting a fresh, inviting vitality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10 – 12 °C. Elegant with shellfish, light fish or as an aperitif that draws the diner back sip after sip.
palate: delicate sweetness, balanced acidity, floral return

name: Paul Aegerter Bourgogne Rouge
description: The 2021 Paul Aegerter Bourgogne Rouge presents a refined interplay of bright red berries and subtle floral nuances supported by gentle oak undertones, all framed in a poised structure that speaks of Burgundian temperament.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature to heighten vibrancy; pairs beautifully with roast chicken, mushroom‑accented dishes, or soft ripened cheeses.
palate: structured yet supple
drinkWindow: to drink now or within 5–10 years

name: Château Grand Portail Bordeaux Rouge
description: A finely balanced expression of Bordeaux from the 2018 vintage elegantly centred on generous Merlot with supporting Cabernet structure offering dark bramble fruit framed by subtle spice and gentle oak nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled; this plush Bordeaux Rouge welcomes roasted lamb or mushroom‑rich dishes with poise.
palate: rich Merlot‑driven fruit with structured Cabernet depth

name: Ano Cero Cabernet Sauvignon la Consulta Mendoza
description: A terroir‑driven Cabernet Sauvignon from La Consulta in Mendoza, offering a graceful fusion of ripe black‑plum and cassis framed by subtle Asian spice and a whisper of savory herbaceousness. The palate is plush yet refined with soft tannins enveloping dark berry fruit and a hint of smoky nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in broad Bordeaux glasses to reveal its fresh fruit and spice layers, ideal alongside grilled red meats or aged cheeses.
aroma: ripe black plum and cassis with Asian spice
palate: plush dark berries with soft tannins and smoky nuance

name: Ano Cero Malbec la Consulta Mendoza
appellation: La Consulta, Valle de Uco, Mendoza
description: From La Consulta in Mendoza this 2024 Malbec Año Cero by Altocedro offers a richly perfumed bouquet of currant and violet with savory dried‑herb notes it unfolds with silky, medium‑to‑full body and inviting dark‑fruit depth that is both lively and beautifully balanced. The wine’s concrete‑fermented pedigree showcases terroir elegance and restrained power.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C ideally with grilled meats or hearty vegetarian dishes its freshness and silky tannins make it a versatile companion.
aroma: currant and violet with dried‑herb nuance
palate: silky medium‑full body, juicy dark fruit
finish: balanced and lingering with gentle tannins

name: La Consulta Select Blend Mendoza
description: A deep ruby Mendoza red wine that exudes finesse and old‑world character, featuring co‑fermented Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo, Petit Verdot, and Syrah. It reveals plush, velvety tannins embraced by layers of ripe black fruit, dried lavender and a whisper of pepper.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in broad glasses to showcase the wine’s elegant structure. Ideal companions include grilled lamb or rich mushroom ragout.
aroma: ripe black fruit, dried lavender, pepper
palate: velvety, layered, harmonious co‑ferment complexity

name: Malbec Gran Reserva
description: This 2019 Altocedro Malbec Gran Reserva, born at altitude in La Consulta within Mendoza’s Uco Valley, unfolds with a presence of ripe plum, cedar and soft violet notes, wrapped in smoky oak from an extended 24‑month French barrel aging. It offers a polished, full‑bodied expression of Malbec marked by depth and finesse, its intricate texture and saline undercurrent offering sustained complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 16–17 °C, perhaps after an hour’s decanting, to appreciate the wine’s layered fruit, refined tannins and lingering finish alongside red meats or aged cheeses.
palate: full‑bodied refined tannins depth

name: Malbec Gran Reserve
description: A richly textured Malbec drawn from century‑old vines in La Consulta, this 2021 Altocedro Gran Reserva exhibits a deep ruby hue and a compelling fusion of black and blue fruit with savory accents. The palate is full‑bodied yet harmoniously balanced, showcasing polished tannins, saline nuance and a refined finish that speaks of its terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at about 15 °C to highlight its vivid fruit and elegant acidity. Pairs beautifully with grilled lamb or aged cheeses.
aroma: blackberry and plum with savory spice
palate: full‑bodied, polished tannins with saline accent

name: Malbec Reserva
description: A sumptuous Mendoza Malbec that weaves together dark plum and blackberry fruit with sensuous mocha and Asian spice notes, offering a plush texture and a gracefully composed presence on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature to reveal its creamy texture and pair with grilled red meats or savory aged cheeses to mirror its dark fruit and chocolate undertones.
palate: plush, creamy, mocha-inflected dark fruit

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Sonoma County
description: A wine of noble bearing with deep black cherry and cassis at its core framed by violet and sage whispers it unfolds in the glass with polished structure and lingering spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperatures to elevate its silkiness, ideal with grilled lamb or aged gouda.
palate: cassiss, blackberry, plum with vanilla bean and clove

name: Domaine Grand Romane Gigondas Cuvee Prestige
description: A refined and generous Gigondas that marries ripe dark berry and subtle plum elements with an undercurrent of pepper and soft herbes de Provence, framed by a gentle kiss of oak that imparts precision without excess.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature around 16 °C, to accompany richly flavored grilled meats or classic Provençal stews.
aroma: ripe dark berries with peppery spice
palate: supple plum fruit with subtle herbes de Provence

name: Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Vaucrains
description: This 2011 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru “Les Vaucrains” from Ambroise carries an aristocratic intensity and vibrant red fruit character emerging from layers of clay‑limestone terroir, refined by patient élevage in new oak. It offers compelling presence while retaining an elegant framework, marrying power and finesse in the classic Burgundy fashion.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 15°C, and pair with richly flavored game or aged regional cheeses to balance its depth and structure.
palate: robust, fruity, slightly spicy

name: Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: This 2009 Ambroise Clos Vougeot Grand Cru unfurls with intense violet‑tinged ruby hues enticing the eye, offering scents of raspberries intertwined with licorice and pepper and a palate that feels rich velvet‑like, opulent and persistent yet balanced with savoury tension
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to 15 °C alongside tender roast lamb or succulent veal—this wine revels in slow revelation yet is approachable now with graceful ageing ahead
palate: rich, opulent, velvety, persistent

name: Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Vaucrains
description: This Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru “Les Vaucrains” from Maison Ambroise 2009 unfolds with formidable depth and refined power, exhibiting poised dark red fruit underpinned by a clay‑limestone minerality. It is robust and opulent yet balanced by structure, evolving from wild berry perfume toward subtle underbrush and leather nuance over time.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15 °C with rich game or aged Époisses or Langres cheese, and allow a decant to reveal its evolving complexity.
aroma: wild red berries evolving to underbrush
palate: robust, fruity, slightly spicy
drinkWindow: drink from 2014 onward; long‑term cellaring possible

name: Amiral de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: Amiral de Beychevelle 2019 presents a cloak of deep, dark ruby purple, the bouquet unfolding layers of black cherry, blackberry and violet with an undercurrent of fine spice. The palate is fresh and balanced, the tannins noble and caressing, leading to a generous yet elegant finish framed by lingering fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 17 °C to enhance its freshness, pairing beautifully with richly roasted meats or savory pâtés.
palate: fresh, balanced, noble tannins

name: Amiral de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: A radiant expression of Saint‑Julien borne of dedicated plots and careful vinification this wine presents floral overtones, spice and vivid freshness balanced by structured yet supple tannins drawn with refined poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C in a large Burgundy‑style glass allow a swirl to reveal red and black fruit nuances. Pair with roast duck or aged comté cheese.
aroma: floral spice and fresh red berries
palate: silky tannins with red fruit and gentle spice

name: Amiral de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: A luminous and refined Saint‑Julien, this 2022 Amiral de Beychevelle greets with a dense brilliant robe and immediate freshness that sets its fruit aglow: poised blackberry, black cherry and cassis threaded with subtle spice and velvety tannins, delivering early appeal tempered by structural promise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool to enhance its poised freshness: ideal with roast lamb, aged duck breast or a mushroom‑dotted cassoulet.
aroma: ripe black cherry, cassis, subtle spice
palate: velvety tannins, fresh vibrant fruit, smooth structure
finish: balanced, long and energetic with a velvety close

name: Domaine Yannick Amirault Bourgeuil la Coudraye
description: Yannick Amirault's 2017 Bourgueil La Coudraye is a rounded Cabernet Franc with fresh red and dark fruit, woodland nuance, and gentle spice. Oak aging adds breadth while the wine retains the croquant freshness of its sandy terrace soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14-16°C with white meats, rabbit, black pudding, or Loire goat cheese.
palate: Round, ample, fresh, softly structured

name: Flare Sparkling Moscatel Do Valencia
description: This non‑vintage Flare Sparkling Moscato from Valencia presents a pale straw hue with delicate effervescence and floral‑fruited aromas of pear, lychee, melon and white blossom brightened by a whisper of spice. The palate offers frothy sweetness tempered by mineral lift and a vivacious, crystalline energy that prevents the finish from feeling cloying.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as a celebratory aperitif or alongside a platter of fresh fruit or light desserts for a playful, refreshing contrast to its sweet charm.
aroma: pear, lychee, melon and white flowers with nutmeg brightness
palate: frothy tropical fruit sweetness enlivened by mineral spice

name: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Pomone
description: This 2018 Bourgogne Rouge Sélection Pomone by Domaine Anne Parent conjures an elegant expression of Pommard terroir distilled into regional Burgundian finesse, revealing vibrant red fruits with a whisper of earthbound complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C to showcase its graceful structure; pair with mushroom ragout or roasted poultry.
palate: ripe cherry, plum, mushroom

name: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Selection Pomone
description: A most refined Bourgogne, this 2018 “Sélection Pomone” by Domaine Anne Parent presents a graceful depth that belies its regional classification, born of venerable Pommard and Premier Cru plots, yielding an elegant yet profound expression of Pinot Noir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 13 °C, in a large-bowled red glass to highlight its red fruit and underbrush nuances; pairs exquisitely with game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: strawberry cherry with subtle rustic underbrush
palate: ripe cherry and plum with a soft tannic grip
finish: elegant, lingering of earth and red fruit

name: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard 1er Cru Croix Noires
description: This 2018 Pommard 1er Cru Les Croix Noires from Anne Parent reveals a delicate perfume of wild red berries and pressed rose petals, unfolding toward a refined structure of silky tannins and well‑integrated oak. The wine’s sophistication speaks of both the textural grace and terroir‑driven depth that define this rare Premier Cru from a revered Burgundian domaine.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool around 15 °C after gentle decanting to coax its floral spice forward. Pair with roast duck, game birds or mushroom‑rich dishes to complement its earthy elegance.
aroma: wild red berries and rose petals
palate: silky tannins with refined structure

name: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard 1er Cru les Epenots
description: A weighty and poised Burgundy bearing a signature of fine-boned red fruit and earthy grace, this 2018 Pommard Premier Cru Les Épenots by Anne Parent unfolds with an expressive bouquet of violet, cherry and morello cherry wrapped in nuanced terroir notes of tilled earth and subtle gunpowder. On the palate it delivers concentrated flesh and sappy structure, underpinned by velvety tannins and a polished, savory finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated at cellar temperature with roasted duck, braised poultry or gamebirds; its graceful power complements rich meats and aged cheeses.
aroma: violet and morello cherry with earthy nuance
palate: fleshy red fruits framed by supple tannins

name: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard 1er Cru les Epenots
description: The 2018 Domaine Parent Pommard 1er Cru “Les Épenots” is a richly structured yet refined red burgundy exhibiting delicious dark cherry and wild strawberry fruit enfolded in perfumed underbrush and subtle floral nuance. It balances concentration with elegance and an underlying soil‑borne character that lends poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15–18 °C with slowly roasted poultry or lightly game‑flavoured dishes to highlight its supple tannins and earthy complexity.
palate: supple red fruit framed by fine tannins

name: Pinot Noir
description: Anthony & Dominic's 2018 Pinot Noir is a fruit-led California expression with bright red berries, supple texture, and softly integrated oak. In three-liter format, it is designed for generous service while retaining Pinot Noir's natural freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly cool and allow the large format to open in the glass; pair with salmon, roast poultry, or herb-roasted pork.
palate: Supple red fruit, gentle oak, fresh acidity

name: Red Wine Napa Valley
description: Arrow & Branch's 2012 Napa Valley Red Wine is a Cabernet Franc-led Bordeaux blend with blackberry depth, floral lift, and a polished mocha undertone. Integrated tannins and lively acidity give the mature wine shape without sacrificing generosity.
sommelierNotes: Give the wine an hour of air and serve with herb-crusted lamb, beef tenderloin, or roasted mushrooms.
palate: Rounded dark fruit, bright acidity, integrated tannin

name: Bodegas Los Astrales Astrales(do Ribera Del Duero)
description: A wine of serious stature drawing from ancient Tinto Fino vines, this 2003 Astrales from Bodegas Los Astrales offers cultivated power and steadfastness with refined Old World restraint, layers of dark fruit interwoven with subtle underbrush and cigar box nuances, delivering a dignified yet expressive presentation.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperatures around 16 °C after gentle decanting to reveal its fragrant depth, pairing best with grilled game, roasted lamb or mature hard cheeses.
palate: structured fruit and cedar spice

description: A full‑bodied southern Rhône blend that feels both grounded and generous, offering warm raspberry and black cherry tones framed by gentle smoke and garrigue notes, with an inviting suggestion of black pepper and licorice on the nose. The wine shows a plush yet structured palate melding ripe fruit intensity with subtle herbal spice, all wrapped in a lingering peppery finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature, around 16–18 °C in a large bowl glass. A fine companion to grilled lamb chops or a Provençal vegetable terrine.
aroma: garrigue and licorice over raspberry and cherry
palate: ripe dark fruit with smoky, herbal depth

description: A refined expression of Fleurie from Château des Bachelards, this 2016 Gamay offers floral elegance anchored in depth. Its fine structure frames vibrant red fruit and delicate violet notes with precision and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 15 °C in a medium‑bowled glass. Perfect with soft‑rind cheeses or simply enjoyed on its own to reveal its finesse.
palate: elegant structure with silk‑textured fruit

name: Château des Bachelards Saint Amour
description: This 2016 Château des Bachelards Saint‑Amour unveils a tapestry of floral and mineral elegance, its garnet hue framing an expressive bouquet of violet and orange blossom. The palate offers a silken yet tension‑filled journey with depth and precision, culminating in a finish of unwavering clarity and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 15 °C, to reveal its fine floral perfume. Pairs elegantly with roast poultry or subtly sauced white meats.
palate: Silken tension with depth

The wine exhibits an understated structure, silky texture and buoyant freshness characteristic of the Côte de Nuits in this vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 15 °C in a tall Pinot Noir glass to reveal the fine red fruit and subtle spice tones; pairs gracefully with roast duck or mushroom risotto.
palate: silky, fresh, minerally

name: 3 Year Kentucky Bourbon Whisky
description: Noble and unvarnished this Kentucky Straight Bourbon offers a refined balance of corn‑sweetness and rye‑driven spice its three‑year journey beginning in American oak then moving into Cabernet Sauvignon wine barrels brings velvet texture and a whisper of dark fruit complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat or with a single large ice cube to reveal vanilla and brown sugar layers, excellent with aged cheddar or chocolate‑dipped dried cherries.
aroma: vanilla bean with candied orange and subtle pink peppercorn
palate: rich maple syrup and toffee underscored by dark cherry and spice
finish: long velvety toast and smoked oak resonance

name: Domaine Bart Marsannay la Montagne
description: The 2019 Domaine Bart Marsannay “La Montagne” is an elegant village‐level Pinot Noir rendered with restraint and clarity, revealing vibrant purple fruit framed by an energetic spine of tannin and a note of mineral nuance from its clay‐rich parcel, offering medium weight with seamless balance and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to awaken its floral and red fruit perfume; pairs beautifully with roast chicken or duck confit to echo its refined structure.
aroma: lavender and violet on spicy purple fruit
palate: silky mid‑palate, cola‑tinged cherry with firm tannins

name: Domaine Bart Marsannay les Ouzeloy
description: This 2020 Marsannay “Les Ouzeloy” from Domaine Bart offers a graceful expression of northern Côte de Nuits with energetic structure and refined concentration. It presents floral lift and tensile power without heaviness nurturing an elegant yet muscular presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to highlight its clarity of fruit and lift, pairing beautifully with mushroom‑accented dishes or roasted meats.
palate: structured concentration, mouthwatering balance

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Barbera D'asti DOCG la Villa
description: An expressive Barbera d’Asti from the storied hills of Incisa Scapaccino, La Villa 2023 is vibrant and vinous with luminous ruby red color and violet hues that beckon the eye. On the nose it reveals fine, intense notes of cherry and wild berries, while the palate is full‑bodied yet balanced, carrying refreshing acidity into a long, pleasant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to accentuate its brisk freshness; pairs beautifully with rich salumi, simple pasta dishes or vitello tonnato.
aroma: fine, intense cherry and wild berries
palate: full‑bodied, fresh, balanced

sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 6‑8 °C in slender stemware to preserve effervescence delightfully paired with light fruit desserts or as a graceful aperitivo.
palate: sweet freshness with creamy mousse

description: The 2021 Benjamin Leroux Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru in magnum presents an elegant and classically structured expression of Chardonnay from one of Burgundy’s most hallowed terroirs. It offers a precise interplay of mineral tension and luminous white fruit framed by a quiet oak presence—a composition both majestic and reserved.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 12–13 °C to reveal its poised minerality and precise citrus core; pairs beautifully with lightly butter‑poached lobster or aged Comté.

palate: precise mineral tension with citrus brightness

name: Bonnamy Cremant de Loire Blanc Brut
description: This Crémant de Loire Blanc Brut NV from Bonnamy presents fine persistent bubbles and a pale yellow color lifted by a delicate interplay of pear and orchard fruit nuances. Earthy whispers from its Chenin Blanc base merge gracefully with floral accents and bright citrus highlights, all given texture by gentle toasty undercurrents from extended lees aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8 to 10 °C as an elegant aperitif or pair with soft cheeses and light fruit desserts to complement its freshness.
palate: fresh orchard fruits with mineral undertone
finish: clean, lingering with gentle nutty echo

name: Bonnamy Cremant de Loire Rose Brut
description: This non‑vintage Crémant de Loire Rosé from Bonnamy offers elegant charm rooted in terroir: delicate wild strawberry and cherry aromas mingle with chalk‑fined freshness and subtle earthiness. The mousse is finely persistent, yielding a luminous pale pink bead and a crisp finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled about 8–10 °C as a festive apéritif or gently pairing with red‑berry sorbet, light shellfish or quiche. Best enjoyed soon, yet shows lovely poise in the near term.
aroma: wild strawberry and cherry with a hint of earth
palate: bright, crisp with fine bead and juicy red‑berry fruit

name: Bonnamy Cremant de Loire Rose Brut
description: An elegant rosé bubble from the Loire Valley this wine unfolds in the glass with fine, persistent bead and a soft coral hue. Bright red berry and citrus threads meet subtle earthiness from Cabernet Franc on a dry yet generous base. The overall impression is refined and inviting, evoking conviviality and timeless tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a flute or tulip glass, as an aperitif or alongside light seafood, delicate poultry or creamy hors d’oeuvres.
aroma: bright red berries with a hint of earthiness
palate: juicy red fruit with citrus freshness
drinkWindow: Drink now to within a few years

name: Cru Barrejats Sauternes
description: A wine of regal Sauternes pedigree from a discreet artisan estate this 2003 Cru Barréjats unfolds with a gracious tapestry of dried fig and candied apricot followed by a whisper of exotic mango and passion fruit, all framed in a silken, liqueur‑rich texture yet tempered with graceful restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in slender stemmed glasses to reveal its regal sweetness, a splendid match for foie gras or delicate fruit‑based desserts, or enjoy contemplatively on its own.
aroma: dried fig, candied apricot, exotic tropical fruit
palate: silken, liqueur‑rich, generous fruit

name: Daniel Bouland Cote de Brouilly Cuvee Melanie
description: From a modest, sunlit parcel atop Mont Brouilly Daniel Bouland’s 2018 Cuvée Mélanie offers vivid red and black fruit framed by expressive mineral nuances and subtle violets, all carried on a refined structure that unites power and elegance.

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Chiroubles Chatenay
description: An elegant and generous Gamay from the slopes of Chiroubles, this wine offers a harmony of ripe red and dark berries woven with floral spice and subtle mineral undercurrents, all framed by a whisper of structure yet buoyant with vivacity.

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Schiste Bellevue
description: Daniel Bouland’s 2018 Morgon Bellevue Schiste is an elegant expression of Gamay that balances vibrant energy and mineral clarity: scented with blue and red berry florals and deep cherry, it is richly textured yet precise, finishing with a long saline and spice-tinged flourish.

description: A thoughtful expression of Morgon from the venerable holdings of Domaine Daniel Bouland, the 2018 Vieilles Vignes Corcelette reveals black and red cherry woven through whispers of violet and fine graphite dust, structured with old‑vine concentration yet lifted by mineral energy from its sandy‑stone soils.

description: Crimson‑tinged and resonant the 2018 Jérôme Castagnier Bonnes‑Mares Grand Cru murmurs of red cherry and bramble on the nose enriched by gentle floral and forest floor hints derived from its storied slopes between Morey‑Saint‑Denis and Chambolle‑Musigny ([bourgognewine.dk](https://bourgognewine.dk/products/bonnes-mares-grand-cru-2018?utm_source=openai)) The palate reveals concentrated depth and structure with firm yet refined tannins underpinning an expansive, lingering, racé finish touched by spice and dark fruit ([hachette-vins.com](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/les-vins/jerome-castagnier-2015-2018-1/201829601/?utm_source=openai))

It conveys an old‑world charm grounded in Tuscan terroir while celebrating the grape’s natural poise.

name: Cave de Saumur Saumur Blanc les Pouches
description: A luminous Chenin Blanc from Cave de Saumur etching vineyards of clay‑silty sands above crayeux tuffeau, this 2023 Les Pouches reveals a pale gold hue with silver glints, offering a poised nose of white peach, Williams pear and acacia‑lime flowers with a subtle flint‑tinge drawn from its terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve quite chilled around 10 °C, ideal as an aperitif or alongside delicate seafood in cream or fresh goat cheese to mirror its purity and finesse.
aroma: white peach and Williams pear with acacia‑lime floral note
palate: light‑bodied, crisp, hint of flintiness

name: Ayni Rose Nature Sparkling
description: This wine offers an elegant mousse with delicate strawberry and peach nuances set against a creamy, toasty backdrop, finishing crisp and finely balanced.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a flute to preserve the pristine effervescence; pairs beautifully with light seafood or festive canapés.
aroma: strawberry and peach interwoven with creamy toast
palate: creamy, fruit-forward with tart cherry and peach

name: Estate Chardonnay
description: The 2018 Chakana Estate Selection Chardonnay from Mendoza offers a graceful expression of ripe stone fruit and citrus framed by gentle oak. It shows an appealing, slightly pulpy mid‑palate texture that balances richness with freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 50–54 °F in tulip‑shaped white wine glasses. It partners beautifully with grilled white fish in lemon butter or creamy poultry dishes.
palate: oily yet fresh, with nectarine and citrus
foodPairings: grilled sea bass with lemon butter

name: Estate Red
description: This 2017 Chakana Estate Red exhibits focused dark berry and plum fruit laced with violet florals, underpinned by subtle exotic spice and mocha nuances, resulting in a poised and elegant expression of high‑elevation Mendoza.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature to highlight its refined structure; try with grilled lamb or mushroom ragù to complement its savory layers.
palate: dark berry and plum with mocha undertones

name: Champagne Camille Saves Carte Blanche Brut 1er Cru
description: An elegant Champagne of character and old‑world poise showing fine interplay of Pinot Noir depth and Chardonnay brightness in each shimmering sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender flute around 8 °C to highlight its lively bead and pair it gracefully with seafood or rich hors d’oeuvres.
aroma: discreet floral and brioche notes emerging to peach, almond, nuts
palate: fresh, poised, subtly tannic in finish

name: Champagne de Sousa Avec le Temps Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut Grand Cru
description: A radiant non‑vintage Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut drawn purely from Grand Cru parcels in Avize, Oger, Le Mesnil and Cramant, it exudes crystalline citrus and blossom lifted by the chalky spine of Côte des Blancs terroir. It balances purity and texture with an elegant richness that unfolds with each sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8–10 °C in a tulip glass to reveal its mineral poise; it partners beautifully with oysters, sushi or delicate cheeses.
aroma: brioche and white flowers with citrus essence
palate: round chalk‑driven minerality with juicy finesse

name: Champagne de Sousa Chemin des Terriors
description: This non‑vintage cuvée is elegantly dense yet vivid in character, offering a refined tapestry of orchard fruits and gentle spice framed by chalk‑anchored minerality, presenting a vinous expression that invites close attention.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 °C in a fine flute or tulip glass to showcase its delicate bead; pairs divinely with oysters, creamy cheeses or light seafood preparations.
palate: fresh orchard fruit, citrus tension, subtle wood note

name: Champagne Edouard Duval Blanc D'eulalie
description: A pale golden and refined expression of Côte des Bar terroir, this Blanc d’Eulalie is crafted from 100 percent Chardonnay vines over fifty years old on the sunlit L’Epicéa parcel it unfolds with gentle fruit and a mineral blossoming that speaks of limestone and oyster fossil soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at circa 10 °C in an elegant flute or tulip glass it pairs beautifully with lobster, light-white fish or delicate shellfish.
aroma: floral with wet stone, red apple, butter
palate: buttered apple, pear, marzipan

name: Champagne Edouard Duval Brut D'eulalie
description: This Champagne exudes an elegant weave of chalk‐inflected minerality and vibrant red fruit energy blending Pinot Noir’s vivid raspberry and pamplemousse with the finesse of Chardonnay from L’Épicéa, all framed in a luminous pale gold sparkle.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C in a slender tulip glass to showcase its fresh fruit brightness and creamy mousse, a refined foil for seafood or soft cheeses.
aroma: raspberry and pink grapefruit over chalky minerals
palate: creamy effervescence with pulpy fruit and lemon‑zesty acidity
finish: fruit‑driven and generous with mineral resonance

name: Champagne Edouard Duval Noir D'eulalie
description: A generous blanc de noirs from Champagne’s Côte des Bar offering noble intensity and supple texture, Noir d’Eulalie unfurls with a refined presence that balances richness and minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in tulip‑shaped flutes or white wine glasses, ideal with shellfish or delicate poultry preparations.
palate: textural depth framed by chalky minerality

name: Champagne G Gruet et Fils Brut Reserve
description: A refined nonvintage Champagne from G Gruet & Fils whose generous expression evokes mature orchard fruits and toasted brioche notes with graceful structure and velvety texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8–10 °C as an elegant aperitif or alongside delicate hors d’œuvres such as smoked salmon or mild cheeses.
palate: creamy texture with vibrant fruit and fine mousse

name: Champagne Hugues Godme Grand Jardins-Le Blanc de Noirs Grand Cru
description: A radiant Champagne born from the Grand Cru terroirs of Verzenay and Verzy this Blanc de Noirs Grand Cru offers a luminous core of dried pear and brioche framed by chalky mineral tension and a whisper of orchard spice. The texture is supple yet poised delivering a svelte mousse and a nervy structure that speaks of vertical energy and refined restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10–12°C in a large white wine or universal Champagne glass to reveal its subtle red fruit tones, perfect with gently spiced lamb tagine or aged Comté.
aroma: dried pear and brioche with gentle spice
palate: supple mousse, orchard fruit, mineral tension

name: Champagne Hugues Godme Jardins Premiers-La Reserve 1ER Cru
description: An elegant blend from Hugues Godmé in Champagne’s Montagne de Reims, Jardins Premiers “La Réserve” Extra‑Brut unveils mineral grace and subtle orchard fruit. The wine offers delicate pear and honeysuckle aromas underpinned by equal parts Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, reflecting biodynamic care. The texture shows refined depth and a lively, precise mousse.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 9 °C in a tulip‑shaped flute to highlight its fresh acidity and minerality; excellent with scallop carpaccio or buttery fish.
palate: mineral and orchard fruit

name: Champagne Hugues Godme Jardins Premiers-Les Terres D'unions 1ER Cru
description: An elegant blend of three Champagne classics  in equal measure this non‑dosé Premier Cru captivates with graceful minerality and subtly ripe orchard fruit, framed by soft brioche and gentle white floral perfume. The texture is finely chiselled sustaining poise and depth throughout.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender flute or white wine glass to showcase its vibrant mousse and tension. Ideal as an aperitif or alongside oysters and light seafood dishes.
palate: mineral‑driven orchard fruit with elegant mousse

name: Champagne Jean Hanotin Brut Tradition Grand Cru
description: Jean Hanotin Brut Tradition Grand Cru NV unfolds with pale golden hues and delicate effervescence, guided by two‑thirds Pinot Noir and one‑third Chardonnay from the Grand Cru terroir of Verzy. It offers an inviting bouquet of red‑fruited and lightly floral notes, all framed by fresh, balanced restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an aperitif, or accompany shellfish or seafood; its finesse and gentle fruit echo beautifully with delicate dishes.
palate: fresh entry with balanced structure and gentle fruit

name: Champagne Jose Dhondt Brut Blanc de Blancs
description: A finely wrought non‑vintage Blanc de Blancs from a small family estate in Oger, this Champagne offers a silken, creamy texture over a precise, chalk‑inflected frame with bright notes of lime, pear and almond.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip flute, it will elevate shellfish, delicate seafood and mild cheeses with its freshness and subtle richness.
palate: creamy texture with chalky minerality and pear

name: Champagne Jose Dhondt Brut Blanc de Blancs
description: This non‑vintage Champagne Blanc de Blancs from José Dhondt offers an elegant expression of Côte des Blancs terroir with bright citrus and floral whispers underscored by a subtle chalky minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in slender flutes to highlight its vivacious acidity and refined bubbles; pairs beautifully with shellfish and soft cheeses.

name: Champagne Leclerc Briant Reserve Extra Brut
description: This Champagne reveals an ethereal pale yellow hue and a luminous fluid appearance, drawing you into a world of almond‑paste, praline and exotic spice. The palate unfolds with tensile lemon acidity atop fleshy, crunchy fruit‑driven depth creating a refined, energetic experience.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10 – 12 °C as a festive aperitif or alongside fusion cuisine featuring pork, lamb or Comté, where its crisp vibrancy and minerality harmonise elegantly.

palate: Crunchy fruitiness underpinned by taut lemon acidity

name: Champagne Paul Launois Contraste #3
description: A striking Blanc de Noirs Extra Brut that marries a vibrant, chalk‑tinged freshness with rounded golden fruit character. The nose unveils a vivid combination of wild berries clementine and yellow plum, enriched by subtle floral honeyed notes and smoked almond nuance. Its palate dances between inviting fruit sweetness and keen minerality, concluding in an elegant salted finish that lingers with precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip flute to highlight its delicate mousse and brisk acidity. A superb match for grilled crustaceans or porcini ravioli with sage butter, its saline tension will lift both seafood and richer autumnal dishes.
aroma: wild berries, clementine, yellow plum, blossom honey
palate: inviting fruit sweetness balanced by crisp acidity and mineral salt
foodPairings: smoked duck breast with apple‑almond salad

name: Champagne Serveaux Fils Carte Noir Brut
description: Serveaux Fils Carte Noire Brut captivates with a luminous golden hue and a refined bead of persistent bubbles, offering an elegant interplay of ripe red fruit and rose petal nuances tempered by a poised minerality. The palate reveals a supple yet vibrant texture with bright acidity, a graceful balance between flesh and finesse, and a lingering finish of subtle almond and citrus lift.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled as an aperitif or alongside shellfish and soft cheeses to complement its delicate charm and refined freshness.

name: Champagne Vazart-Coquart Brut Reserve Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs
description: An elegant non‑vintage Blanc de Blancs that expresses the chalky terroir of Chouilly with supple, airy texture and a harmonic weave of white stone fruits and gentle brioche, finishing with a mineral poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled as an aperitif or alongside refined shellfish and delicate crustacean dishes to complement its citrus‑lifted freshness.
aroma: white stone fruit and light pastry nuance
palate: supple, airy texture with citrus and brioche elements

description: Philippe Charlopin-Parizot's 2014 Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes is a savory, firmly built Pinot Noir with dark cherry, earth, and woodland spice. Old-vine depth is balanced by the vintage's freshness, leaving a long, composed finish.
sommelierNotes: Decant gently for sediment and serve at 15-16°C with duck, venison, or beef bourguignon.
palate: Layered fruit, firm fine tannin, fresh core

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes Morceaux
description: This 2015 Vieilles Vignes "Morceaux" from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot is an elegant expression of Gevrey‑Chambertin, offering a nuanced interplay of red‑fruit vibrancy and forest‑floor depth. It presents an engaging tension between earthy notes and cherry fruit framed by fine-grained structure and poised concentration.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 14 °C, and enjoy with roasted game birds or a classic Coq au vin, allowing the wine’s layered character to complement rich, savory flavors.
palate: balanced red fruit, refined tension

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay les Echezots
description: Philippe Charlopin-Parizot's 2014 Marsannay Les Échezots is a ripe, expressive Pinot Noir with ruby fruit, floral lift, and carefully integrated oak. The palate combines generosity with a fresh acid spine and enough structure for a savory close.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature with roast pork, duck confit, or mushrooms; a brief decant will help the mature fruit open evenly.
palate: Juicy fruit, polished oak, fresh acidity

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay Montchenevoy
description: An elegant and harmonious Pinot Noir that reveals dark berry fruit wrapped in subtle woody spice, graceful structure and refined balance hinting at gentle evolution in bottle.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to unveil its purity alongside roasted game or classic Burgundy fare.
palate: round yet precise with fine tannins

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay Montchevevoy
description: This 2015 Marsannay “En Montchenevoy” from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot reveals a poised elegance rooted in its limestone soils, with delicate aromas of peony and rose unfolding into subtly spiced red fruit. The palate is refined and lithe with silky tannins and an airy finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in a Burgundian stem to showcase its floral nuance and graceful structure; pairs beautifully with roasted poultry or herb‑scented charcuterie.
palate: silky red fruits, refined structure

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Pernand Vergelesses Blanc les Pins
description: Philippe Charlopin-Parizot's 2014 Pernand-Vergelesses Blanc Les Pins is a Chardonnay of bright citrus, wet stone, and restrained beeswax. Its high-toned acidity and firm mineral backbone frame a mature but still energetic white Burgundy.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 11-12°C and give the bottle a modest amount of air; pair with shellfish, sole, asparagus risotto, or soft cheese.
aroma: Lemon zest, wet stone, matchstick, beeswax
palate: Bright citrus, firm acidity, mineral depth

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Pernand Vergelesses Blanc les Pins
description: This 2015 Pernand‑Vergelesses Blanc “Les Pins” from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot offers a graceful core of white orchards and bright citrus enlivened by a whisper of oak and a refined mineral undercurrent, capturing the subtle tension of its clay-limestone hillside origin. The wine carries a measured breadth without heaviness and the signature freshness of Côte de Beaune Chardonnay elevated by finesse and precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at about 50 °F in a tulip glass to emphasize its clarity and detail, and consider pairing with poached white fish in herb butter or creamy goat cheeses to complement its texture and mineral lift.
aroma: white orchard fruit with subtle oak and mineral hints
palate: fresh, focused, with citrus and gentle wood spice

name: Margaux
description: An accomplished Margaux from Château Cantenac Brown, the 2018 vintage offers a sumptuously structured expression of firm black fruit and spicy underpinning, framed with fine-grained tannins and a poised sense of balance that reflects a rare precision in this warm yet refined year.

aroma: black cherry, raspberry, licorice, cedar, exotic spice
palate: densely concentrated, energetic yet structured

name: Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits Saint Georges aux Allots

It moves with grace and reserve inviting contemplation rather than showmanship.

aroma: Elegant red fruit and gentle spice
palate: Supple bramble‑fruit core with refined texture

name: Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits Saint Georges aux Saint Juliens
description: This 2019 Domaine Chicotot Nuits‑Saint‑Georges “Aux Saint Juliens” is an elegant, finely structured Pinot Noir displaying delicate floral perfume and bright cherry fruit, with lace‑like precision and a persistent, refined presence

palate: lace‑like cherry and floral interplay

name: Classic Dry Cider
description: This nonvintage Classic Dry Cider from The Cider Farm is an elegant expression of orchard craftsmanship: it blends five traditional English cider apples with an American tart Liberty apple to deliver firm tannins, balanced acidity, and a clean, refreshing finish. The palate reveals nuanced complexity and crisp effervescence while showcasing the character of true cider apples rather than dessert varieties.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its tactile tannins and vibrant acidity; pairs beautifully with aged cheeses or herb‑crusted poultry.
aroma: bright orchard fruit with subtle tannic earthiness
palate: structured yet refreshing with nuanced apple depth

name: Cyser Cider
description: This lightly golden Cyser bridges the old‑world charm of tart cider apples with the sweet floral richness of locally sourced honey, yielding a semi‑dry libation that still carries approachable warmth. The palate offers a gentle interplay of orchard‑fresh apple and mellow honey that unfolds with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve just chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its honeyed aromatics and pair with nutty cheeses or roasted poultry.
palate: balanced tart‑sweet, soft honeyed texture

name: Dabinett Cider
description: This organically crafted cider from The Cider Farm expresses the noble Dabinett apple in a rare single‑variety form enhanced by select additions of Liberty, Chisel Jersey, and Porter’s Perfection, creating a semi‑dry, floral elegant offering with lush caramel and tropical undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its floral freshness and medium‑plus tannin structure, ideal with creamy cheeses or spiced pork dishes.
aroma: tropical and floral with rich caramel
palate: fresh apple juice, guava and cooked pineapple with balanced medium‑plus tannins

name: Oak Aged Cider
description: A refined and elegant cider gently matured in medium‑toast American oak, offering a soft interplay of vanilla warmth and subtle toast complexity rooted in heritage apple character.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in slender stemware alongside roast poultry or mushroom‑topped fare to uplift the cider’s nuanced oak and orchard fruit interplay.
palate: balanced orchard fruit framed by oak

name: Oak Aged Cider
description: This oak‑aged cider unfurls with whisperings of vanilla and toast, the subtle medium‑toast American oak enriching the orchard fruit’s brightness in an elegant, wine‑like embrace. It carries a refined clarity and balance that evokes a polished Chardonnay nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip or white wine glass to highlight its gentle oak nuance: an ideal match for roast poultry or creamy alpine cheeses.
palate: bright orchard fruit with toast

name: The Cider Farm Belgian Saison
description: This Belgian‑style farmhouse cider unfolds with layered citrus and spice on a background of restrained apple tannins, reminiscent of old‑world saison but refined by orchard depth and aromatic subtlety.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip or stemmed glass to enhance its citrus‑spice perfume and pair with soft cheeses or light seafood fare.
palate: tannic apple with bergamot and gentle hop lift

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Apple Brandy Aged Five Year
description: Opulent and orchard‑driven this aged apple brandy offers a refined amber hue and envelops the senses in a gentle embrace of orchard fruit framed by warm oak and bourbon‑barrel whispers each bottle uniquely carries the story of its single‑barrel origin.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a tulip glass to appreciate its depth or with a single small ice cube to soften its warmth; pairs elegantly with rich pâté or aged cheeses.
aroma: deep orchard fruit and charred oak
palate: fruit‑forward with bourbon‑barrel warmth

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Apple Brandy Aged Two Years
description: A quietly beguiling Wisconsin apple brandy that speaks in orchard whispers, aged two years in charred bourbon barrels with the subtle presence of wild apple wood from the farm, offering a soft interplay of barrel echoes and orchard purity.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a tulip glass to admire its clarity and gentle warmth, or use as a refined substitute for bourbon in classic cocktails.
palate: soft apple flesh and gentle oak spice

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Pommeau Aged Three Years
description: A refined and mellow fortified apple aperitif, this Pommeau from The Cider Farm is crafted in Wisconsin using their orchard‑grown cider apples and apple brandy, patiently aged for three years to reveal a soft golden hue and layered orchard fruits
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a small tulip glass as a refined aperitif or alongside nut‑forward desserts, aged cheeses, or fruit tarts

name: Bourgogne Blanc

name: Domaine Collotte Marsannay les Boivins

The wine shows the hallmarks of its Puyméras terroir, delivering warmth and balance with old‑world restraint.

name: Armand/epeneaux Auxey Duresses 1ER Cru Rouge
description: An elegant and poised Pinot Noir offering from Comte Armand, its 2017 Auxey‑Duresses Premier Cru marries refined red and black fruit flavors with a streak of mineral energy and supple structure, its intensity underpinned by a subtle frame of new oak.

name: Domaine des Epeneaux Auxey Duresses Rouge

The palate is broad and virile yet refined, showing depth, malted undertones and waves of sappy structure.

palate: precise, intense, energetic dark fruit

description: This 2017 Daniel Bouland Côte‑de‑Brouilly Cuvée Mélanie opens with a richly poised bouquet of blackberry and wild berries underlined by savory dark chocolate and subtle licorice nuances, balanced by smoky mineral undertones from its volcanic hillside terroir. The palate is full‑bodied yet fresh with lush dark fruit framed by compelling structure and restrained tannins lingering into a layered, spice‑tinged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled at cellar temperature, alongside rabbit in wine sauce or softly poached egg pairing, to accentuate its fruit‑driven depth and mineral elegance.

palate: lush dark fruit, structured, restrained tannins

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Pre Jourdan
description: This 2020 Daniel Bouland Morgon “Pré Jourdan” unfolds with profound black‑fruit intensity evocative of cassis and ripe cherry tempered by an undercurrent of smoke and gentle salinity. The wine’s structure is supple yet vivid with fine tannins caressing the palate alongside a subtle hint of salted caramel and a smoky echo.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to highlight the fruit clarity and smoked nuances; pairs beautifully with roasted pork, earthy mushroom dishes or charcuterie boards.
palate: velvety, fine‑tannin structure with salted caramel nuance

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Vieilles Vignes Corcelette
description: A graceful and perfumed Morgon from Daniel Bouland’s historic Corcelette enclave, the 2017 Vieilles Vignes displays focused energy and depth, woven with red and black cherry, floral lift and mineral precision. It offers structure and cachet, with an undertow of dusty earth and savoury nuance that suggest long‑term refinement.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below ambient cellar temperature in thin crystal, pair with roast pork, aged cheeses or wild mushrooms to complement its perfume and fine tannin.
aroma: red and black cherry with dried flowers and mineral dust
palate: velvety, concentrated, perfumed core with fine tannins

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Heart Arrow Ranch
description: This single‑vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon from biodynamic Heart Arrow Ranch in Mendocino’s Eagle Peak exudes dark, structured elegance, with layers of blackberry, cassis and plum threaded through graphite and forest‑floor nuances in a deep purple‑black hue
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 62 °F in a large Burgundy‑style glass; pairs beautifully with herb‑crusted lamb or mushroom‑scented sauces
palate: structured with balanced acidity and complex fruit
finish: persistent with mineral and black pepper spice

name: Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon Heart Arrow Ranch
description: This 2018 Dashe Cellars Heart Arrow Ranch Cabernet Sauvignon evokes the noble austerity of old‑world claret, with concentrated notes of black cherry and cassis underpinned by graphite and violets, all framed by mineral tension and velvety structure. sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar cool temperatures it partners gracefully with roasted duck or venison stew to highlight its silken texture and mineral clarity
palate: silken red fruit with fine acidity

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Gevrey Chambertin en Champs
description: This Gevrey‑Chambertin En Champs 2017 from Domaine Cheurlin‑Noëllat reveals an alluring mélange of kirsch and cassis, underpinned by subtle whispers of spice and smoke, evolving toward a more complex bouquet of humus and forest floor with graceful age. The palate is refined and supple, bolstered by fine‑grained tannins and lively freshness, carrying through to a balanced, gently grilled finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool warmth to best display the wine’s energy and purity; pair with game birds in red wine jus or roasted veal with wild mushrooms.
aroma: kirsch and cassis with smoke and humus
palate: supple, refined, fine‑grained tannins with freshness

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Grands Echezeaux
description: A grand‑cru of noble bearing this Grands‑Échézeaux 2023 from Domaine Georges Noëllat unfurls with purity of fruit and mineral clarity: plummy black cherry and underbrush waft from the glass, supported by refined spice and smoky nuance. The palate is dense yet elegant, structured by fine tannins that carry impressive depth and tension into a lingering, poised conclusion.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C after decanting to reveal the wine’s textural finesse and layered aromatics; superb with veal or lamb but will reward cellar time over the next decade.
palate: velvety yet structured, with mineral clarity

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Meursault 1er Cru aux Cras
description: The 2018 Domaine Georges Noellat Meursault 1er Cru “Les Cras” emerges from a rare northerly parcel bordering Caillerets and overlooking Volnay Santenots, presenting a luminous golden hue and a refined aromatic veil of white orchard fruit, citrus and delicate florals, underpinned by a whisper of toasted almond and stone. On the palate it reveals an elegant interplay of creamy texture and vibrant acidity, balanced by fine mineral tension that lends a lingering sense of finesse and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 10–12 °C in a tulip glass to highlight its citrus nuances; pairs exquisitely with butter‑poached lobster, creamy poultry preparations or aged Comté.
aroma: white orchard fruit, citrus blossom and subtle toast
palate: creamy yet vibrant with mineral tension

description: This Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru “Aux Boudots” from Domaine Georges Noëllat 2017 unfolds with refined red and black fruit accented by subtle earth and spice layers maintaining a poised elegance rooted in its Côte de Nuits heritage.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperatures around 14 °C after decanting to reveal its delicate structure; pairs beautifully with earthy game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes.
palate: silky red and black fruit with fine tannic backbone

name: Domaine Georges Noellat Nuits-Saint-Georges 1ER Cru aux Boudots Rouge
description: A richly textured Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru from Domaine Georges Noëllat the 2015 Aux Boudots offers soaring aromas of black cherry violet and orange blossom layered over seamlessly integrated oak, unfolding into a vivid framed palate of sappy red‑berry fruit and saline minerality.

description: An elegant expression of Nuits‑Saint‑Georges aux terraced slopes of Aux Cras, this 2017 from Domaine Georges Noëllat unfurls with pure cherries, cassis and violet perfume that remains primally fresh, held by a structured yet inviting mid‑palate of succulent red fruit and refined tension.

name: Domaine Meo-Camuzet Corton Perrieres Grand Cru
description: This 2021 Corton Grand Cru Les Perrières by Domaine Méo‑Camuzet unfurls in refined layers bold yet elegant, melding polished black fruit, restrained spice and a tensile mineral spine that speaks of its stony hillside terroir with poise and promise.

name: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Pommard 1er Cru les Epenots
description: A noble and concentrated Pinot Noir from the revered Pommard 1er Cru Les Épenots, the 2018 vintage by Domaine Nicolas Rossignol delivers rich dark fruit intensity with an undercurrent of graphite and subtle spice, balanced by purposed structure and grand cru‑like depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature around 16 °C; pairs beautifully with veal, lamb or game in rich sauces, and should continue gaining complexity through the next decade.
aroma: layered dark cherry and blackcurrant with graphite and spice
palate: concentrated yet refined, ripe black fruit framed by polished tannins

name: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Volnay 1er Cru Cailleret
description: A pale‑ruby Burgundian of ethereal grace finely woven from Volnay’s famed Cailleret terroir this 2019 Volnay 1er Cru 'Cailleret' from Nicolas Rossignol unfurls in the glass with peony, sweet berry, blood orange and spice nuances delivering freshness and depth in measured harmony, the texture silky, the structure elegant and lace‑like.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature, pair with roast poultry or delicately braised veal, perhaps a mushroom fricassee enhancing the wine’s floral‑mineral poise.
palate: fresh density with silky tannins

name: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Volnay 1er Cru les Taillepieds
description: From a lofty perch above Volnay this 2018 Volnay 1er Cru Les Taillepieds offers a refined texture of ripe red berries framed by a steely mineral thread, its noble lineage revealed in the nuanced grace of its tannins and the polished structure that unfolds elegantly in the mouth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 55–57 °F in a large Burgundy stemware to showcase its poised complexity: pairs exquisitely with herb‑crusted roast duck or a wild mushroom risotto.
palate: structured elegance with fine tannins

name: Domaine Nicolas Rossignol Volnay 1er Cru Ronceret
description: This 2019 Volnay Premier Cru “Ronceret” from Domaine Nicolas Rossignol unfolds with an elegant interplay of dark and red berry fruit—blackberry, cassis and boysenberry—framed by subtle mandarin energy and an underlying mineral clarity, offering a sense of precision with generous volume on the mid‑palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature in burgundy stemware to highlight the freshness and fine tannins. Pairs beautifully with lightly roasted duck or mushroom‑driven dishes.
palate: fleshy dark and red fruit, sensual, balanced

name: Domaine Olivier Merlin Bourgogne Rouge
description: This 2022 Bourgogne Rouge from Domaine Olivier Merlin captures an assured brightness in lighter cherry and raspberry underpinned by a gentle earthiness and a streak of fine tannin. It presents a poised charm that feels both energetic and elegantly restrained, reflecting the minerality of its Mâconnais origins while remaining classically poised in Burgundy style.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to highlight its purity alongside simply seared salmon, roast chicken with mushrooms or a creamy herb risotto.
palate: fine purity with gentle earthiness and subtle tannin
finish: clean and refreshing with slight structure

On the palate it is deftly poised, inviting root‑beer‑like vanilla and peppermint nuances anchored by a whisper of espresso‑mocha, closing with soft caramel and banana‑bread sweetness.

The finish is long and rich with lingering dark chocolate and brown sugar.

finish: Long, rich and persistent with dark chocolate and brown sugar

name: Spirits Gustaf Navy Strength Gin
description: A fearless Navy‑strength gin crafted grain‑to‑glass from winter rye in Minnesota this Gustaf offers bold and spirited balance. The aromatic weave of meadowsweet thyme cucumber and vanilla frames an assertive rye‑driven backbone for an engaging contemporary profile.

aroma: meadowsweet thyme cucumber with a rye‑grain hum
palate: fiery rye warmth softened by fennel citrus pepper and vanilla
finish: dry herbal linger with gentle anise warmth

name: Spirits Gustaf Navy Strength Gin
description: This fearless Navy‑strength gin stands proudly at 114 proof offering a bold tapestry of botanicals. Delicate lavender and juniper weave through hints of yuzu‑like citrus while fennel and licorice add spicy depth and enduring character.

The result is an elegant expression that balances grain‑forward complexity with warming spice.

palate: butter‑smooth, smoked ham, balsa wood

name: Spirits Solveig Gin

It unfurls restrained floral aromas of lavender and violets interwoven with dark plum, clove and a whisper of dark chocolate, while fine tannins lend a velvety texture and underlying structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in a large Burgundy glass to invite the perfume, and pair with roasted lamb, duck with cherry glaze or wild mushroom risotto to complement its spice and depth.
aroma: lavender and violets with dark plum and clove
palate: brooding black plum, mocha, spice, velvety tannins
foodPairings: slow‑roasted lamb with rosemary and garlic

sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 16 °C in medium‑bodied Bordeaux or Burgundy style glasses: a fine match for roast lamb or aged Manchego cheese.

description: The 2016 Château de Fosse‑Sèche Arcane Saumur Blanc is a Chenin Blanc shaped by silex‑rich soils that impart a pronounced mineral clarity and an aromatic whisper of white flowers, quince and honey, unfolding with elegant restraint and old‑world precision. Its presence is refined rather than flamboyant, offering subtle power and crystalline focus that speak of its Loire terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled at 9–12 °C after gentle aeration to open floral lift and mineral drive; pair with oysters, sole meunière or goat cheeses to echo the wine’s freshness and subtle floral tones.

name: Weingut Franz Hirtzberger Riesling Hochrain Smaragd
description: A crystalline expression of Wachau Riesling, this 2018 Hochrain Smaragd offers lifted notes of yellow stone fruit and mandarin zest with a whisper of floral perfume, all cast in an elegant, finely chiselled frame of layered extract and poised energy. The texture is silky, the fruit precise, driven by a tensile acidity that carries through to a long, seamless finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C to reveal its intricate fruit and mineral finesse, ideal alongside refined fare such as buttered sole, veal scaloppine or subtly spiced river fish.
aroma: yellow stone fruit and mandarin zest with floral perfume
palate: silky texture, layered extract, poised energy
finish: long, seamless with white fruit nuances

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Alexander Valley
description: A velvety Cabernet Sauvignon from Gabrielle Ashley’s 2020 Alexander Valley, presenting a refined ribbon of black fruits and subtle forest‑floor nuances allied to gentle oak tones
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in a large Bordeaux glass, and pair with grilled lamb or aged cheddar to accentuate the wine’s understated complexity
palate: smooth black fruit framed by soft oak

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve Napa Valley
description: This 2020 Gabrielle Ashley Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve from Napa Valley presents a richly fruit‑driven elegance reflecting its appellation and the skillful hand at Precision Wine Company. Generous notes of black cherry, cassis and plum unfold alongside subtle vanilla and toast from harmonious oak aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature to preserve freshness. Pair with grilled red meats or aged cheese for a classic Napa expression.
aroma: ripe black cherry and cassis with vanilla and toasty oak
palate: lush plum and blueberry fruit wrapped in velvety tannins
finish: long silky finish with spice and toast

description: The 2017 Galil Grenache Noir from Upper Galilee unfolds gracefully with a fine weave of red cherry, wild raspberry, and subtle rose petal, framed by an earthy spice through elegant restraint and old‑world poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 14–16 C to highlight its bright fruit and floral nuance; pair with rustic lamb stew or wild mushroom risotto to complement its spice and earth tones.
palate: wild raspberry with earthy spice

name: Merlot
description: This 2017 Merlot from Galil Mountain presents vivid black plum and blackberry fruits set against a weaving of clove, tobacco leaf and herbal underbrush, held together by soft framing oak. The wine wears its Mediterranean heritage with grace, offering depth without brashness.
sommelierNotes: Best served at cellar cool temperatures, it finds harmony with grilled lamb chops or herb‐roasted pork shoulder, where its savory and fruit tones complement each other.
palate: smooth blackberry with clove and gentle oak

name: Mountain Winery Blanc de Noir
description: This Blanc de Noir 2020 from Galil Mountain Winery unfurls with a pale, ethereal hue and a finely wrought texture showcasing hand‑picked Pinot Noir pressed as a delicate white. It evokes gentle orchard fruit framed by a whisper of citrus and refined minerality, all carried with a poised, lithe elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its brightness, pairing beautifully with light fish dishes or creamy soft cheeses.
palate: light texture with mineral lift

name: Winery Rose

sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an aperitif or alongside light summer fare such as goat cheese salads or grilled seafood, its refreshing acidity offering a refined counterpoint
palate: crisp wild red fruits with citrus lift

It reveals an underpinning of velvet tannins and a harmonious texture.

sommelierNotes: Serve slightly decanted at cellar cool, alongside hearty fare such as slow‑braised lamb or cassoulet, to temper its structure while highlighting its savory fruit

palate: rich dark‑fruit core, firm yet ripe tannins

name: Ancestral Red
description: This Gen5 2024 Ancestral Red presents a richly inviting tapestry of wild blackberry and blueberry pie accented by gentle mocha and baking spices, offering a creamy texture and velvety finish that recalls classic old‑world reds with modern California generosity.

palate: firm yet velvety red fruit with savory grip

name: Bulzai Ginjo Sake
description: Manotsuru “Bulzai” Ginjo presents a crisply invigorating expression of Niigata’s refined sake tradition, showing delicate citron and yellow apple on the forefront, with a whisper of white pepper and stony mineral, precisely balanced in its ginjo clarity. The nama‑chozo method lends it a bright, zest‑laden energy that evokes the sea‑cooled mornings of Sado Island.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a narrow wine glass to highlight its delicate fruit and peppery minerals; ideal alongside salt‑grilled fish or subtly butter‑seared seafood.
palate: white pepper and mineral briskness

name: Bulzai Ginjo Sake
description: This Bulzai Ginjo sake is a refreshing artisan expression from Niigata’s Sado Island crafted by Obata Shuzo under the Manotsuru label, elegantly balancing bright yellow apple and citron notes with a fine mineral undertone. It offers a refined sense of clarity and that invigorating zest one expects from a meticulously milled Ginjo sake.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its bright fruit and spiced nuance; pairs gracefully with delicate sushi or simply butter‑sauteed white fish.
aroma: yellow apple, citron, subtle tropical fruit
palate: refreshing minerality with touch of white pepper

name: Countless Visions Nigori Sake
description: This Junmai Ginjo Nigori sake presents itself with an inviting cloudy hue and a light sweetness tempered by gentle sourness. Fragrant notes of starfruit and guava unfold to a refreshing and animated style.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled after an attentive shake to reincorporate the sediment, paired with lively dishes such as spicy Mexican tacos or delicate fried fish to complement its creamy spice.
palate: light sweetness with gentle acidity

name: Countless Visions Nigori Sake
description: A luscious Junmai Ginjo Nigori sake, Manotsuru “Countless Visions” unfurls a veil of creamy cloudiness that gives way to a softly sweet, refreshingly balanced palate. Tropical whispers of starfruit and guava interlace with delicate anise and melon, culminating in a gentle spicy crescendo that evokes quiet contemplation.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled after a gentle shake to harmonize its fine rice sediment; beautifully suited to contrast spicy cuisine or to accompany light fried fish for an elegant interplay of texture and flavor.
palate: silky sweet fruit with anise‑melon nuance

name: Crane Junmai Sake
description: An elegant junmai sake from Niigata’s artisanal Obata Shuzo, Manotsuru Crane exudes a refined purity with whispering stone fruit and delicate pistachio nuances framed by a subtle kiss of white chocolate. The palate is poised and silky, offering a gently structured yet graceful presence. This is a sake of understated harmony and old‑world craft.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to appreciate its soft fruit elegance or at cool room temperature to reveal deeper umami layers: an excellent companion to sukiyaki or lightly seared tofu.
palate: silky, balanced, subtly nutty

name: Crane Junmai Sake
description: This Manotsuru Crane Junmai offers an elegant serenity that whispers of Niigata’s blessed terroir, the clarity of its soft Sado waters reflected in delicate nuances of pistachio and forest floor, its texture pure and unadorned, a quiet embodiment of craftsmanship without flourish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to reveal its soft umami and gentle nuttiness, a harmonious companion to sukiyaki, tamagoyaki or subtly seasoned grilled tofu.
palate: mild umami with soft nutty tones
drinkWindow: Drink now to enjoy its fresh aromatic clarity

name: Crane Karakuchi Sake
description: This honjoso sake, Manotsuru Crane Karakuchi, offers a beautifully refined experience with bright citrus florals and delicate almond undertones a silkily elegant expression of Niigata’s dry ‘‘karakuchi’’ tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to reveal its taut freshness or gently warmed to enhance its smooth silkiness ideal with simply seasoned poultry or light seafood.
palate: silky, elegant, dry

name: Daimyo Honjozo
description: This Honjozo from Manotsuru speaks in an understated yet confident voice its gentle refinement reflecting the four treasures—rice, water, brewers and terroir—that define its origin. The palate is dry and soft yet subtly engaging, with airy harmony rather than overt bravado. Drinking it brings a whisper of Sado Island’s misty morning in every sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly warmed or at room temperature to reveal its delicate umami and soften the gentle driest finish.
palate: dry with gentle umami balance

name: Demon Slayer Tokubetsu Honjozo Sake
description: An exceptionally dry Tokubetsu Honjozo from Obata Shuzo’s Manotsuru label this sake presents a crisp clarity with echoes of dried fruit, aromatic herbs and a faint whisper of cinnamon drawing the palate into its penetrating austerity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to enhance its sharp precision and pair with delicate raw seafood or subtly seasoned rich meats to balance the intense dryness.
palate: crisp super‑dry austerity

name: Demon Slayer Tokubetsu Honjozo Sake
description: A rigorously dry Tokubetsu Honjozo from Obata Shuzo on Sado Island, “Demon Slayer” delivers a poised mid‑weight presence carving through notes of dried fruit, meadow herbs and a brush of cinnamon, culminating in a crystalline, minerally air of perfection.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled or softly warmed to reveal elegant herb and dried fruit nuances; perfect alongside sushi, fresh sashimi and oysters.
palate: meadow herb and cinnamon mid‑weight

name: Kanadel Orikarami Junmai Daijinjo Sake
description: This Manotsuru Kanadel Orikarami Junmai Daiginjo reveals a delicate interplay of fizz and finesse with lifted notes of ripe melon and lychee carried on a whisper of effervescent silk. It unfolds with gentle aromatic grace and finishes with subtle persistence like the echo of a haiku's last line.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip glass to preserve its soft sparkle, ideally alongside light seafood or elegant hors d’oeuvre to accent its airy clarity.
palate: light, bouncy, gently fizzy

name: Lucky Toki Junmai
description: A pure‑rice junmai imbued with the spirit of Sado Island and the auspicious toki crane it honors. Gentle stone‑fruit and soft white‑chocolate tones glide across a sleek, dry frame with subtle depth, inviting contemplative sipping.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or gently warmed to reveal both its delicate fruit‑like nuance and warming umami: pairs beautifully with sashimi or lightly seasoned fare.
palate: elegant, dry, refined

name: Maho Daijinjo Sake
description: This Manotsuru Maho Daiginjo presents a lush aroma of ripe peach, orange peel and faint cotton‑candy perfume, giving way to an elegantly mild yet racy entry and a refined, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or about 15 °C in a wine glass to reveal its layered nuance: its gentle elegance pairs beautifully with creamy caviar or rich hors d’oeuvres.
palate: elegant, mild and racy entry

name: Pure Bloom Junmai Ginjo
description: Manotsuru “Pure Bloom” Sweet Junmai Ginjo presents a delicate floral elegance grounded in refined sweetness, a soft and light expression born of Sado Island’s pure waters and artisanal tradition. Subtle notes of lychee and cherry blossom drift through its graceful texture, lingering with creamy nuance and poised transparency.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its floral and sweet character, pairing beautifully with creamy desserts or light tomato‑based salads.
palate: soft, elegant sweetness with white chocolate undertones

name: Pure Bloom Junmai Ginjo Sake
description: An ethereal and delicate junmai ginjo that feels like spring in a glass offering a soft, floral aroma threaded with subtle lychee and honeyed warmth, its gentle 12 percent spirit carrying a light, elegant sweetness floating on a whisper of vanilla and milk.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its floral nuance: pairs beautifully with light appetizers and fresh summer desserts.

palate: elegant, lightly sweet with vanilla‑milk whispers

description: The 2018 Antinori “Antica Estate” Cabernet Sauvignon from Townsend Vineyard unfolds with a noble presence, offering finely etched dark fruit and mineral-driven intensity supported by a muscular yet poised frame sourced from Napa Valley’s Atlas Peak. The wine reveals a sense of refined structure, with a balance of brooding black fruit, tension and notable depth.

description: An elegant Napa Valley Chardonnay of refined mountain pedigree, the Antica Estate “A26” 2019 unfolds with subtlety and depth, offering delicate notes of stone fruit and citrus framed by gentle oak nuances. The wine is poised and structured, its texture creamy yet lithe, conveying a harmonious balance that speaks of both place and lineage.

aroma: stone fruit and citrus with gentle oak nuances
palate: creamy yet lithe texture with balanced fruit and freshness

name: Margaux de Brane Margaux
description: A generous second wine fashioned with graceful poise and Bordeaux charm. Vibrant dark berry scents framed by subtle toast hint at effortless accessibility and understated refinement. The palate is harmonious, buoyed by smooth structure and pliant tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at around 16 °C. Pairs beautifully with duck breast, roasted mushrooms or charcuterie on a crisp evening.
aroma: blackberry and blackcurrant with subtle toast
palate: round, balanced and fleshy with silky tannins

description: The 2016 Marina Coppi "Marine" Favorita Colli Tortonesi emerges with graceful harmony its pale straw hue revealing delicate orchard fruit and meadow herb aromas. On the palate it is refined and rounded offering fine texture with flavors of ripe peach, herbal lift and subtle mineral undertow.

palate: slightly mineral with Mediterranean herb nuance
finish: long clean finish with balsamic echo

name: Bellmunt Negre

sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 14 °C in a Burgundy glass to highlight its vivacity; pairs beautifully with grilled vegetables, mild cured meats or rustic charcuterie.

description: This Morey‑Saint‑Denis 2019 from Maxime Cheurlin‑Noëllat embodies the finesse and unsentimental precision of the Côte de Nuits. It reveals rich red fruit framed with a whisper of herbs and violet perfume, all backed by poised structure and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C to coax out its elegance. Pair with delicate game birds, wild mushrooms, or mild soft‑ripened cheeses to complement its red‑berry nuance.

Its texture is seamlessly balanced between power and elegance reflecting the stony minerality of Monti in Chianti.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool temperature in large-bowled glasses to allow the plush yet erect tannins to unwind. Ideal with richly seasoned braised meats or aged cheeses.
aroma: dark berries with vanilla and licorice
palate: velvety yet structured with wild cherry and mineral depth
finish: long and balanced with mocha and subtle oak
